gen-gf-grandstander-gf-voces: Grandstander's lines hold a constant width, bold and loudly expressive. Voces, the sans-serif text face, brings modest thick-thin contrast against those flat heading strokes, and that shift is the pair's best quality.
gen-gf-gugi-fs-amulya: Amulya feels thoroughly modern, its sans-serif curves keeping generous gaps and lowercase of moderate height. Gugi's tall, uniform-stroke letters then add the swagger, while Amulya keeps the text moving.
gen-gf-gugi-fs-roundo: Big, blunt and a bit cheeky: Gugi's tall lowercase nearly climbs to capital height, with terminals sliced to let each counter breathe. Gugi grabs attention, while Roundo, a geometric sans, keeps small counters clear.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-allerta: Gugi builds its capitals from lines of constant thickness, and its lowercase climbs nearly as high. But Allerta's wide, loose tracking and prominent x-height make a sans-serif paragraph drift by without strain.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-asimovian: Approachable is the first word for Asimovian, whose tall lowercase bodies hold one stroke width beneath Gugi's louder heading. Gugi makes the loud statement, while Asimovian carries the sans-serif text quietly.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-basic: Gugi is a display face with a single-depth, engraver-like cut and lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals. Basic, though, keeps text clean and professional, with only a gentle step up from small letters to capitals.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-cal-sans: Approachable and modern, Cal Sans runs a single stroke width throughout. Its short ascenders and tall x-height make long stretches of text feel compact and friendly, a quiet foil for Gugi's bold heading.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-carlito: Gugi draws each glyph with one simple tip, its tall lowercase nearly touching the capitals, while Carlito holds the sans-serif text. Carlito's tight spacing and small-looking capitals stay compact beneath that louder heading.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-farro: Farro is approachable, with compressed ascenders and no stroke contrast at all. Farro would sit nicely a size or two below Gugi's tall, bold heading, whose curves match its stems.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-geist-mono: Gugi's lowercase climbs nearly to capital height, with sliced-open terminals that let each curve breathe. Geist Mono's fixed-width, code-style rigor is the sharpest thing here, set against a heading that never holds back.
